raw_response:
Useful references for the implementation-hiding problem

These seven candidates provide access-control designs, an alternative module mechanism, and public compiler code. The application suggestions below are transfers to the stated problem, not claims that they were implemented or validated in Swift.

1. Scala 2 enclosing-template private and private[this]
https://scala-lang.org/files/archive/spec/2.11/05-classes-and-objects.html
Scala's explicit enclosing-template and object-local access modifiers provide a compiler-checkable model for hiding an implementation member without using its source file as the protection boundary. Ordinary private permits companion access, while private[this] additionally restricts the receiver; those distinctions need deliberate treatment for extensions.

2. C++ private members and explicit friendship
https://timsong-cpp.github.io/cppwp/n3337/class.access
C++ private members and explicit friend grants distinguish implementation-only access from intentional cooperation between related types even when their declarations share a translation unit. The rule is type-wide, and inaccessible names can remain visible to lookup, so extension isolation and completion filtering need separate decisions.

3. Java SE8 private accessibility
https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se8/html/jls-6.html
Java's private-access rule supplies a precise static boundary that prevents a separate neighboring top-level class from using another class's implementation members merely because both are in one file. Its top-level-class boundary also grants access among nested classes, and it does not model Swift extensions.

4. C# private accessibility and partial declarations
https://www.ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-334_4th_edition_june_2006.pdf
C# combines private access tied to a declaring type with partial declarations, providing a model for keeping implementation organization flexible while denying access from unrelated neighboring types. Partial blocks form one type, so this approach would share privacy privileges across those blocks.

5. OCaml module signatures
https://ocaml.org/manual/4.00/ocaml-4.00-refman.pdf
An OCaml signature can expose only selected operations of a local structure and make omitted helpers unnameable through that interface, offering a separate compiler-enforced implementation compartment within one source file. Constrain the structure at definition rather than leave an unrestricted implementation binding available; this approach introduces explicit interfaces.

6. Eiffel secret and selective feature export
https://www.ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-367_2nd_edition_june_2006.pdf
Eiffel's explicit client sets separate secret implementation features from features available to chosen collaborating classes, providing a compiler-enforced alternative to granting every declaration in a file access. Selective export includes clients' descendants, and the rules distinguish qualified from unqualified calls.

7. Clang's access-checking implementation
https://llvm.googlesource.com/clang/%2B/master/lib/Sema/SemaAccess.cpp
Clang's public semantic-analysis code provides a concrete implementation reference for storing declaration access, walking enclosing declaration contexts, and accepting or rejecting a private-member reference. Its C++-specific ownership and friendship rules need adaptation; the opened revision was not built or executed.

Timing and verification: Scala's object-local modifier is dated to 2007-03-09 by its specification changelog; N3337 is confirmed by the 2012-01-16 WG21 editor report; Java SE8's opened PDF is dated 2015-02-13; the C# and Eiffel standards are June 2006 editions; and the OCaml manual is dated 2012-07-26. The exact Clang master revision remains date-unknown. The later live C# and Eiffel documentation was recorded separately and was not used to backdate those standards.

I would use these references to distinguish a declaration's narrow implementation scope from intentional sharing with related code, then make code completion consult the same accessibility decision. Whether multiple extensions share one type-wide privilege or each has its own boundary remains an explicit design choice.

Search limitation: the unauthenticated grep.app API attempt was inaccessible. The Clang source was discovered through public web search and opened on its public code host; this was code-through-web fallback, not successful native code search. Both primary N3337 PDF attempts timed out, so its access-control text was read in a versioned HTML rendering and its date checked against the original editor report.
